note: This unit's vocabulary spans the Weimar Republic, National Socialism, the Second World War, the division of Germany, and reunification — the shared background knowledge most C1 reading texts about modern Germany assume.

examples.de: Die deutsche Geschichte des 20. Jahrhunderts ist geprägt von zwei Weltkriegen, einer Diktatur und der Teilung des Landes.
examples.en: 20th-century German history is shaped by two world wars, a dictatorship, and the division of the country.

note: Germany's first parliamentary democracy, 1919–1933 — named after the city where its constitution was drafted, not a place it was governed from.

examples.de: Die Weimarer Republik bestand von 1919 bis 1933.
examples.en: The Weimar Republic existed from 1919 to 1933.

note: The ideology and regime of the NSDAP under Hitler, 1933–1945 — also referred to as "das Dritte Reich" or "die NS-Zeit." No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Nationalsozialismus führte Deutschland in den Zweiten Weltkrieg.
examples.en: National Socialism led Germany into the Second World War.

note: A form of government with no free elections and power concentrated in one person or party — applies to both Nazi Germany and, later, the GDR.

examples.de: Eine Diktatur kennt keine freien Wahlen.
examples.en: A dictatorship has no free elections.

note: 1939–1945 — began with the German invasion of Poland, ended with Germany's unconditional surrender.

examples.de: Der Zweite Weltkrieg endete 1945 mit der Kapitulation Deutschlands.
examples.en: The Second World War ended in 1945 with Germany's surrender.

note: The systematic genocide of six million European Jews by Nazi Germany — also referred to as "die Shoah." No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Holocaust gilt als eines der größten Verbrechen der Menschheitsgeschichte.
examples.en: The Holocaust is considered one of the greatest crimes in human history.

note: Someone who actively opposed the Nazi regime, often at great personal risk — from Widerstand (resistance), pairing with kämpfen.

examples.de: Die Widerstandskämpfer des 20. Juli 1944 planten ein Attentat auf Hitler.
examples.en: The resistance fighters of 20 July 1944 planned an assassination attempt on Hitler.

note: The split into two states, 1949–1990 — a consequence of the postwar occupation zones hardening into the Cold War border.

examples.de: Die Teilung Deutschlands dauerte von 1949 bis 1990.
examples.en: The division of Germany lasted from 1949 to 1990.

note: One of the four zones (American, British, French, Soviet) Germany was divided into after 1945 — the origin of the later East–West split.

examples.de: Nach dem Krieg wurde Deutschland in vier Besatzungszonen aufgeteilt.
examples.en: After the war, Germany was divided into four occupation zones.

note: Deutsche Demokratische Republik — the East German state, 1949–1990. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die DDR wurde 1949 gegründet und bestand bis 1990.
examples.en: The GDR was founded in 1949 and existed until 1990.

note: Bundesrepublik Deutschland — the West German state from 1949, and reunified Germany's official name since 1990. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die BRD entstand im selben Jahr wie die DDR.
examples.en: The FRG came into being the same year as the GDR.

note: The decades-long standoff between the Western and Soviet blocs, with divided Germany as one of its central stages. No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Kalte Krieg prägte die deutsch-deutschen Beziehungen jahrzehntelang.
examples.en: The Cold War shaped German-German relations for decades.

note: 1961 — the GDR sealed the border between East and West Berlin overnight. No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Mauerbau 1961 trennte Ost- und Westberlin.
examples.en: The building of the Wall in 1961 separated East and West Berlin.

note: 9 November 1989 — the event that opened the path to reunification. No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Mauerfall 1989 markierte das Ende der deutschen Teilung.
examples.en: The fall of the Wall in 1989 marked the end of the German division.

note: 3 October 1990, when the GDR formally joined the FRG — now Germany's national holiday. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Wiedervereinigung wurde am 3. Oktober 1990 vollzogen.
examples.en: Reunification was completed on 3 October 1990.

note: West Germany's rapid postwar economic recovery in the 1950s. No natural plural.

examples.de: Das Wirtschaftswunder brachte Westdeutschland in den 1950er Jahren wirtschaftlichen Aufschwung.
examples.en: The economic miracle brought West Germany an economic upswing in the 1950s.

english: coming to terms with the past
note: The ongoing collective process of confronting and processing the Nazi period — a famously untranslatable German compound. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Vergangenheitsbewältigung ist bis heute ein zentrales Thema der deutschen Erinnerungskultur.
examples.en: Coming to terms with the past remains a central theme of German remembrance culture today.

note: The practices — memorials, anniversaries, education — through which a society keeps its history present. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die deutsche Erinnerungskultur zeigt sich in zahlreichen Gedenkstätten und Jahrestagen.
examples.en: German remembrance culture is expressed in numerous memorials and anniversaries.

note: Someone who personally lived through a historical event and can testify to it firsthand — increasingly rare for the Nazi era.

examples.de: Ein Zeitzeuge berichtete den Schülern von seinen Erlebnissen während des Krieges.
examples.en: A contemporary witness told the students about his experiences during the war.

note: Short for Staatssicherheit — the GDR's state security service, notorious for surveilling its own citizens. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Stasi überwachte Millionen von DDR-Bürgern.
examples.en: The Stasi surveilled millions of GDR citizens.

note: Helping someone escape, especially across the inner-German border — Fluchthelfer risked prison or worse. No natural plural.

examples.de: Fluchthilfe über die innerdeutsche Grenze war streng verboten.
examples.en: Assistance in fleeing across the inner-German border was strictly forbidden.

note: The forced removal of a population from a territory — most often, in this context, the postwar expulsion of ethnic Germans from Eastern Europe.

examples.de: Nach dem Krieg kam es zur Vertreibung von Millionen Deutschen aus Osteuropa.
examples.en: After the war, millions of Germans were expelled from Eastern Europe.

note: Living abroad, unable or unwilling to return home for political reasons — many writers and intellectuals went ins Exil during the Nazi period. No natural plural in this sense.

examples.de: Viele Schriftsteller gingen während der NS-Zeit ins Exil.
examples.en: Many writers went into exile during the Nazi period.

note: The systematic targeting of a group for its identity or beliefs — die Verfolgung von Juden, Sinti und Roma, politisch Andersdenkenden.

examples.de: Die Verfolgung politisch Andersdenkender begann bereits 1933.
examples.en: The persecution of political dissidents began as early as 1933.

note: A place, often a former camp or site of persecution, preserved and open to visitors as a memorial.

examples.de: Die Gedenkstätte erinnert an die Opfer des Konzentrationslagers.
examples.en: The memorial site commemorates the victims of the concentration camp.

note: The yearly recurrence of a historical date — der Jahrestag des Mauerfalls, der Kriegsendes.

examples.de: Der Jahrestag des Mauerfalls wird jedes Jahr gefeiert.
examples.en: The anniversary of the fall of the Wall is celebrated every year.

note: A period of fundamental political or social transformation — used especially for 1989/90.

examples.de: Die Jahre 1989/90 waren eine Zeit des politischen Umbruchs.
examples.en: The years 1989/90 were a time of political upheaval.

note: The academic field studying events still within living memory — roughly, German history since 1945 or 1949. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Zeitgeschichte untersucht Ereignisse, die noch im lebendigen Gedächtnis vieler Menschen liegen.
examples.en: Contemporary history examines events still within many people's living memory.
